blocks.html:
READING PASSAGE 3

You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 27-40, which are based on Reading Passage 3 below.

Termite Mounds

Could the vast towers of mud constructed by insects in sub-Saharan Africa hold the key to our energy-efficient building of the future?

Paragraph A (Q27):

A To most of us, termites are destructive insects which can cause damage on a devastating scale. But according to Dr Rupert Soar of Loughborough University's School of Mechanical and Manufacturing Engineering, these pests may serve a useful purpose for us after all. His multidisciplinary team of British and American engineers and biologists has set out to investigate the giant mounds built by termites in Namibia, in sub-Saharan Africa, as part of the most extensive study of these structures ever taken.

Paragraph B (Q28):

B Termite mounds are impressive for their size alone; typically they are three metres high, and some as tall as eight metres have been found. They also reach far into the earth, where the insects ‘mine' their building materials, carefully selecting each grain of sand they use. The termite's nest is contained in the central cavity of the mound, safely protected from the harsh environment outside. The mound itself is formed of an intricate lattice of tunnels, which split into smaller and smaller tunnels, much like a person's blood vessels.

Paragraph C (Q29):

C This complex system of tunnels draws in air from the outside, capturing wind energy to drive it through the mound. It also serves to expel spent respiratory gases from the nest to prevent the termites from suffocating, so ensuring them a continuous provision of fresh, breathable air. So detailed is the design that the nest stays within three degrees of a constant temperature, despite variations on the outside of up to 50 °C, from blistering heat in the daytime to below freezing on the coldest nights. The mound also automatically regulates moisture in the air, by means of both its underground ‘cellar', and evaporation from the top of the mound. Some colonies even had ‘chimneys' at a height of 20 m to control moisture loss in the hottest regions of sub-Saharan Africa.

Paragraph D (Q30):

D Furthermore, the termites have evolved in such a way as to outsource some of their biological functions. Part of their digestive process is carried out by a fungus, which they 'farm' inside the mound. This fungus, which is found nowhere else on earth, thrives in the constant and optimum environment of the mound. The termites feed the fungus with slightly chewed wood pulp, which the fungus then breaks down into a digestible sugary food to provide the insects with energy, and cellulose which they use for building. And, although the termites must generate waste, none ever leaves the structure, indicating that there is also some kind of internal waste-recycling system.

Paragraph E (Q31):

E Scientists are so excited by the mounds that they have labelled them a 'super organism' because, in Soar's words, “They dance on the edge of what we would perceive to be cool or, if you're too cold, you need to thrive: that's called homeostasis.” What the termites have done is to move homeostatic function away from their body, into the structure in which they live. “As more information comes to light about the unique features of termite mounds, we may ultimately need to redefine our understanding of what constitutes a ‘living' organism.”

Paragraph F (Q32):

F To reveal the structure of the mounds, Soar's team begins by filling and covering them with plaster of Paris, a chalky white paste based on the mineral gypsum, which becomes rock-solid when dry. The researcher then carves the plaster of Paris into half-millimetre-thick slices, and photographs them sequentially. Once the pictures are digitally scanned, computer technology is able to recreate complex three-dimensional images of the mounds. These models have enabled the team to map termite architecture at a level of detail never before attained.

Paragraph G (Q33):

G Soar hopes that the models will explain how termite mounds create a self-regulating living environment which manages to respond to changing internal and external conditions without drawing on any outside source of power. If they do, the findings could be invaluable in informing future architectural design, and could inspire buildings that are self-sufficient, environmentally friendly, and cheap to run. “As we approach a world of climate change and temperatures rise,” he explains, “there will not be enough fuel to drive air conditioners around the world.” It is hoped, says Soar, “that the findings will provide clues that aid the ultimate development of new kinds of human habitats, suitable for a variety of arid, hostile environments not only on the earth but maybe one day on the moon and beyond.”

questionGroups.bodyHtml:
Questions 27–33

Reading Passage 3 has seven paragraphs A–G.

Choose the correct heading for each paragraph from the list of headings below.

Drag a heading from the list and drop it onto the correct paragraph's answer box on the left.

List of Headings
i. methods used to investigate termite mound formation
ii. challenging our assumptions about the nature of life
iii. reconsidering the termite's reputation
iv. principal functions of the termite mound
v. distribution of termite mounds in sub-Saharan Africa
vi. some potential benefits of understanding termite architecture
vii. the astonishing physical dimensions of the termite mound
viii. termite mounds under threat from global climate change
ix. a mutually beneficial relationship

Questions 34–37

Label the diagram below.

Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.

Questions 38–40

Do the following statements agree with the claims of the writer in Reading Passage 3?

In boxes 38–40 on your answer sheet, write

  • YES if the statement agrees with the claims of the writer
  • NO if the statement contradicts the claims of the writer
  • NOT GIVEN if it is impossible to say what the writer thinks about this

38 The termite mound appears to process its refuse material internally.

39 Dr Soar's reconstruction involves scanning a single photograph of a complete mound into a computer.

40 New information about termite architecture could help people deal with future energy crises.

passageNotes.label: Paragraph A
passageNotes.text: 对多数人而言，白蚁是极具破坏性的昆虫，但拉夫堡大学的鲁珀特・索尔（Rupert Soar）博士认为，这种害虫或许能为人类提供帮助。他带领英美跨学科团队，对非洲撒哈拉以南地区纳米比亚的巨型白蚁丘展开迄今最全面的研究。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph B
passageNotes.text: 白蚁丘的规模本身就令人惊叹 —— 通常高 3 米，部分可达 8 米，且深入地下（白蚁从中 “开采” 建筑材料，精心筛选每一粒沙子）。蚁巢位于丘体中央腔室，免受外界恶劣环境影响；丘体由复杂的隧道网络构成，隧道不断分支变细，类似人类的血管系统。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph C
passageNotes.text: 这套复杂的隧道系统有多重功能：从外部吸入空气，利用风能驱动气流循环；排出巢内废弃呼吸气体，避免白蚁窒息，确保新鲜空气持续供应；设计精密到能将巢内温度控制在 ±3℃范围内（外界温差可达 50℃，白天酷热、夜晚严寒）；还能自动调节空气湿度（通过地下 “地窖” 和丘顶蒸发），部分白蚁群甚至在撒哈拉以南最热地区建造 20 米高的 “烟囱” 控制水分流失。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph D
passageNotes.text: 此外，白蚁进化出 “外包部分生理功能” 的生存策略 —— 其消化系统的部分工作由一种真菌完成，这种仅存在于白蚁丘内的真菌，在稳定适宜的环境中生长。白蚁将轻微咀嚼的木浆喂给真菌，真菌将其分解为可消化的含糖食物（供白蚁获取能量）和纤维素（供白蚁筑巢）；且白蚁产生的废物从不排出丘体，暗示存在内部废物回收系统。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph E
passageNotes.text: 科学家将白蚁丘称为 “超级生物体”，索尔解释：“它们处于生存的临界状态，这种自我调节能力称为内稳态（homeostasis）。” 白蚁将内稳态功能从自身转移到居住的结构中。随着白蚁丘独特特征的更多信息被发现，人类可能最终需要重新定义 “生命体” 的构成。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph F
passageNotes.text: 为揭示白蚁丘结构，索尔团队先向丘体填充熟石膏（干燥后变硬），再将其切成半毫米厚的薄片，依次拍照；数字化扫描后，通过计算机技术重建丘体的复杂三维图像，这些模型使团队能以前所未有的细节绘制白蚁建筑结构。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph G
passageNotes.text: 索尔希望这些模型能解释 “白蚁丘如何在不依赖外部能源的情况下，构建自我调节的生存环境，应对内外环境变化”。若能实现，研究成果将为未来建筑设计提供宝贵参考，启发打造自给自足、环保且低成本运行的建筑。他解释：“随着气候变化、气温上升，全球将没有足够燃料驱动空调。” 研究还希望为 “开发新型人类栖息地” 提供线索，适用于地球各类干旱恶劣环境，甚至未来的月球等外星环境。

questionExplanations.sectionTitle: 1. 段落标题匹配（Questions 27–33：Choose the correct heading）

items.text:
（1）题目 27：Paragraph A
答案：iii（reconsidering the termite’s reputation，重新评估白蚁的名声）
解析：Paragraph A 开篇指出 “多数人认为白蚁破坏性强”，随后转折 “但索尔博士认为其有利用价值”，核心是 “重新看待白蚁的名声”，与标题 iii 一致，因此选 iii。

（2）题目 28：Paragraph B
答案：vii（the astonishing physical dimensions of the termite mound，白蚁丘惊人的物理规模）
解析：Paragraph B 聚焦 “白蚁丘高度（3-8 米）、地下深度、复杂隧道结构”，核心是 “物理规模”，与标题 vii 一致，因此选 vii。

（3）题目 29：Paragraph C
答案：iv（principal functions of the termite mound，白蚁丘的主要功能）
解析：Paragraph C 详细说明隧道系统 “通风、控温、调湿” 等功能，核心是 “功能阐述”，与标题 iv 一致，因此选 iv。

（4）题目 30：Paragraph D
答案：ix（a mutually beneficial relationship，互利共生关系）
解析：Paragraph D 描述 “白蚁喂养真菌，真菌为白蚁提供食物和建材”，核心是 “白蚁与真菌的互利关系”，与标题 ix 一致，因此选 ix。

（5）题目 31：Paragraph E
答案：ii（challenging our assumptions about the nature of life，挑战我们对生命本质的认知）
解析：Paragraph E 提出 “白蚁丘是超级生物体”“可能需重新定义生命体”，核心是 “挑战生命本质认知”，与标题 ii 一致，因此选 ii。

（6）题目 32：Paragraph F
答案：i（methods used to investigate termite mound formation，研究白蚁丘结构的方法）
解析：Paragraph F 详细介绍 “填充石膏、切片、拍照、计算机建模” 的研究步骤，核心是 “研究方法”，与标题 i 一致，因此选 i。

（7）题目 33：Paragraph G
答案：vi（some potential benefits of understanding termite architecture，理解白蚁建筑术的潜在好处）
解析：Paragraph G 讨论研究对 “未来建筑、外星栖息地” 的启发，核心是 “潜在应用价值”，与标题 vi 一致，因此选 vi。

items.text:
（1）题目 34：network of \___\___ helps to give the termites a constant supply（\___\___网络帮助白蚁获得持续供应）
答案：tunnels（隧道）
解析：定位 Paragraph C 中 “This complex system of tunnels draws in air from the outside... ensuring them a continuous provision of fresh, breathable air”，“隧道系统” 是空气供应的关键，因此答案为 “tunnels”。

（2）题目 35：a constant \___\___ supply and to maintain a limited temperature range（持续的_\___\__供应，且维持有限的温度范围）
答案：air（空气）
解析：定位 Paragraph C 中 “ensuring them a continuous provision of fresh, breathable air... the nest stays within three degrees of a constant temperature”，“持续供应的是空气”，因此答案为 “air”。

（3）题目 36：cellar to aid control of \___\___ levels in mound（地窖帮助控制丘体内的_\___\__水平）
答案：moisture（湿度）
解析：定位 Paragraph C 中 “The mound also automatically regulates moisture in the air, by means of both its underground ‘cellar’”，“地窖用于调节湿度”，因此答案为 “moisture”。

（4）题目 37：top of the mound permits （丘顶允许）
答案：evaporation（蒸发）
解析：定位 Paragraph C 中 “and evaporation from the top of the mound”，“丘顶通过蒸发调节湿度”，因此答案为 “evaporation”。

items.text:
（1）题目 38：The termite mound appears to process its refuse material internally.（白蚁丘似乎在内部处理废物）
答案：YES（正确）
解析：定位 Paragraph D 中 “although the termites must generate waste, none ever leaves the structure, indicating that there is also some kind of internal waste-recycling system”，“废物不排出，暗示内部处理”，与题干描述一致，因此判定为 YES。

（2）题目 39：Dr Soar’s reconstruction involves scanning a single photograph of a complete mound into a computer.（索尔博士的重建过程涉及将完整白蚁丘的单张照片扫描到计算机中）
答案：NO（错误）
解析：定位 Paragraph F 中 “carves the plaster of Paris into half-millimetre-thick slices, and photographs them sequentially. Once the pictures are digitally scanned, computer technology is able to recreate complex three-dimensional images”，“需扫描多张切片照片，而非单张完整照片”，与题干描述矛盾，因此判定为 NO。

（3）题目 40：New information about termite architecture could help people deal with future energy crises.（关于白蚁建筑术的新信息可能帮助人类应对未来能源危机）
答案：YES（正确）
解析：定位 Paragraph G 中 “the findings could be invaluable in informing future architectural design, and could inspire buildings that are self-sufficient, environmentally friendly, and cheap to run... as climate change and temperatures rise, there will not be enough fuel to drive air conditioners”，“启发节能建筑，应对燃料短缺”，与题干描述一致，因此判定为 YES。
